annotations.actionTaken: Cast Surgical Extraction (likely paying 2 life with Phyrexian mana) before playing a land for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Polluted Delta first, fetch a Swamp (or Island), then cast Surgical Extraction paying {B} to save 2 life points. Alternatively, play Undercity Sewers (tapped) and then cast Surgical Extraction, though the fetch-into-Swamp line saves the most life.

annotations.description: Gem3P Timmy used Surgical Extraction to target Griselbrand, which is already the only copy in the opponent's graveyard. While removing Griselbrand from the graveyard prevents Goryo's Vengeance reanimation, all three copies of Goryo's Vengeance are already in the graveyard, so there's no way for the opponent to reanimate Griselbrand anyway. Meanwhile, the opponent has key cards that could still matter: Ephemerate (3 copies in graveyard, could have copies in hand/library enabling blink combos with Solitude), Solitude (2 in graveyard, could have more in library), or even Atraxa, Grand Unifier (in graveyard but also potentially in library). Targeting Goryo's Vengeance itself would be redundant since all copies are milled. However, extracting something like Ephemerate or Solitude would strip the opponent of their primary interactive/value engine pieces that might still be in their library. That said, Griselbrand is an enormously powerful threat if somehow reanimated, and being cautious about it isn't unreasonable - it's just that the reanimation spells are already gone.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Griselbrand with Surgical Extraction
annotations.betterLine: Target Ephemerate or Solitude with Surgical Extraction to strip remaining copies from the opponent's hand and library, since all Goryo's Vengeances are already in the graveyard making Griselbrand reanimation impossible through that route

annotations.description: Gem3P Timmy has a Ruin Crab-less board (it likely died or was removed earlier) but has Polluted Delta and Undercity Sewers in hand, plus Flooded Strand as a choice to activate. The opponent has 40 cards in their graveyard out of a typical 60-card deck, meaning they're very close to being milled out. By not cracking Polluted Delta now (or playing Undercity Sewers/Flooded Strand from hand), Timmy is missing landfall triggers if Ruin Crab were still on board. More importantly, Timmy is passing the turn without playing a land at all - they have Undercity Sewers and Flooded Strand in hand but chose not to play either one, missing a land drop entirely. Even without Ruin Crab, missing a land drop in a mill deck that wants to cast spells is suboptimal. Additionally, the Polluted Delta on the battlefield could be cracked to enable Archive Trap if the opponent searches, but keeping it uncracked is defensible. The main issue is not playing a land from hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without playing a land, keeping Undercity Sewers and Flooded Strand in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Undercity Sewers (tapped land with surveil) to make the land drop, improving mana development and getting a surveil trigger to find more mill spells. Could also play Flooded Strand for an untapped fetch option.

annotations.description: Fatal Push can only destroy creatures with mana value 2 or less normally, or 4 or less with Revolt. Psychic Frog has mana value 2, so it will be destroyed regardless. However, the sequencing is slightly suboptimal: Gem3P Timmy should have sacrificed Polluted Delta first (or played Flooded Strand and cracked it) before casting Fatal Push to enable Revolt. While Revolt doesn't matter for Psychic Frog (MV 2), it would matter if the opponent responded by flashing in a higher-MV creature or if circumstances changed. More importantly, cracking the fetch first would trigger any future landfall effects and thin the deck. The bigger issue is that Gem3P Timmy is spending their only removal spell on a 1/2 Psychic Frog when they're playing a mill deck at 13 life. The opponent has 40 cards in their graveyard out of roughly 60, meaning they've milled a huge portion already. However, Psychic Frog can grow with discards, has combat damage card draw, and can gain flying - it's a real threat that could close the game. The Fatal Push is reasonable here, but casting it in the main phase rather than at end of opponent's turn or in response to an attack/pump gives the opponent full information and mana to respond. With the opponent having Island and Hallowed Fountain untapped, they could have countermagic available.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Fatal Push targeting Psychic Frog during own precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Wait to cast Fatal Push during the opponent's turn (e.g., during their upkeep, combat, or in response to a pump activation) to deny them information and potentially catch them tapped out. Alternatively, crack Polluted Delta first to enable Revolt as a precaution before casting Fatal Push.

annotations.description: Gem3P Timmy cast Hedron Crab before activating Shelldock Isle. The opponent has only 6 cards left in library, and Shelldock Isle's condition is met (a library has 20 or fewer cards). The exiled card under Shelldock Isle could potentially win the game immediately (e.g., if it's a Fractured Sanity or Archive Trap, it could mill the remaining 6 cards). By casting Hedron Crab first, Timmy uses the one untapped blue source (likely needed for Shelldock Isle activation cost of {U}), potentially delaying the Shelldock Isle activation. Additionally, even if mana works out, checking Shelldock Isle first is better sequencing since it could end the game before needing to commit the Hedron Crab. With only 6 cards in the opponent's library, Shelldock Isle's free spell could be immediately lethal, making Hedron Crab unnecessary.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Hedron Crab for {U} before checking/activating Shelldock Isle
annotations.betterLine: Activate Shelldock Isle first (paying {U} from an untapped land) to play the exiled card for free. If the exiled card mills the remaining 6 cards, the game is won immediately. If not, then proceed with Hedron Crab and landfall triggers to finish the job.

annotations.description: Gem3P Timmy has Hedron Crab on board, Undercity Sewers in hand, and Polluted Delta + Shelldock Isle available to activate. Playing the land and cracking Polluted Delta would trigger Hedron Crab twice for 6 additional mills, potentially finishing the opponent's library this turn. Additionally, Shelldock Isle's activation condition is met (opponent's library ≤20 cards), and the hidden card could be cast for free. Passing without using any of these resources gives the opponent an extra turn to potentially find answers.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without playing land or activating any abilities, assuming opponent was already fully milled out.
annotations.betterLine: Play Undercity Sewers (triggering Hedron Crab to mill 3), then activate Polluted Delta to fetch a land (triggering Hedron Crab again for 3 more mills), and consider activating Shelldock Isle to cast the exiled card for free, ensuring the opponent is completely milled out this turn.
